cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Let Them Think They Won
cards.instruction: Protect someone’s confidence by hiding how much you softened the challenge, changed the terms, or withheld an advantage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Congratulations on winning the cake contest, Mum.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your cake isn't on the judging table.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. It stayed in the kitchen where I can admire it privately.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You still beat seven cakes that had every intention of winning.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 congratulates and A5 cites other cakes, but actual authority mostly in generic prefixes rather than A means of protecting Mum confidence.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 winner spots absence and infers concession, a plausible concern about gifted victory.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 doubt to emphasize genuine remaining competition rather than disclose A withdrawal motive.

specificity.evidence: A1 Mum cake contest winner and B2 judging table establish family and result.
